### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors recent behavior and repeated narrow preferences. These motivate testing history dependence, without treating sensitivity as proof of intent. (2) Existing margins measure training-pair separation. Their dependence on score scale prevents interpreting larger margins as better rankings. (3) Compatibility and satisfied needs remain partly unobserved. Diagnostics must distinguish explicit evidence from missing information.

**Related work.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* [1] motivates checking whether order matters. Availability-aware shuffling [2] shows why uncontrolled permutations can mislead. (2) Sampled-ranking research [3] establishes that sampled and catalog rankings can disagree. Consequently, catalog audits should supplement the pinned selection metric. (3) TREC’s recommendation definitions [4] separate complements from compatibility. They support explicit unknown states when specifications are absent.

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Proposed measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| History dependence | Training histories | Controlled deletion and shuffling | Dependence, not intent |
| Ranking quality | Pinned validation candidates | HR@10 and target ranks | Sampled-candidate performance |
| Practical relevance | Titles/descriptions | Supported/conflicting/unknown flags | Missing prerequisites do not establish nonownership |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Controlled history-evidence adapter — 5/8/3.** Originality: + combines controlled perturbations with the required adapter; − perturbation analysis is established [1,2]. Potential: + identifies actionable model dependencies; − cannot establish causal user preferences. Difficulty: + requires no retraining; − careful masking and matched controls are necessary.
2. **Recency residual scorer — 4/7/5.** Add a learned mixture of SASRec scores and recent-item embedding affinity. Originality: + tests a focused explanation of feedback; − resembles established recency models. Potential: + directly changes ranking; − may amplify recency bias. Difficulty: + small scoring change; − requires training and predictor-writer synchronization.
3. **Specification evidence flags — 5/6/6.** Extract explicit model/interface/dimension statements [4]. Originality: + grounds explanations in source spans; − structured compatibility assessment already exists. Potential: + exposes unsupported associations; − sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: + deterministic extraction is feasible; − reliable conflict rules require substantial validation.

### Selected idea: controlled history-evidence adapter

At 0% progress, establish trustworthy diagnostics before spending training budget on architectural changes. Preserve the existing six metrics, but attach valid counts and mark empty estimates unavailable.

For each evaluated history, compare baseline scores with recent-history deletion, older-history deletion, and seeded equal-count random deletions. Separately shuffle the item multiset while fixing the latest item. Preserve original seen-item exclusions and candidate sets throughout.

```
freeze model; enter evaluation mode
for history, fixed_candidates in permitted_validation:
    score baseline and controlled variants
    record hit@10, target rank, top10 overlap
aggregate paired effects within category; macro-average
return metrics, metric_definitions
```

Keep `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and its loader-only entry point; expose validation auditing separately through a host-compatible hook. Use `view.model` for mode restoration. Bootstrap users within categories, report uncertainty and unmatched controls, and select checkpoints solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [2](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042), [3](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651), [4](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html).

idea.description: Extend the required diagnostic adapter with controlled history perturbations that measure model dependence on recent interactions, older history, and sequence order. Preserve existing embedding and training-margin probes while distinguishing them from validation ranking measurements.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests weak use of current interests, but existing probes cannot establish whether the model uses recent evidence or whether changing that dependence would improve recommendations. At initial research progress, controlled measurements provide a feasible foundation for subsequent scoring changes without asserting unobserved intent, ownership, or satisfaction.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the actual module through view.model; save and restore its training state. Use view.log2feats and view.predict_score without assuming a particular encoder architecture. Retain existing metric names and add valid counts and availability indicators; unavailable category breakdowns remain empty. Loader-derived probes may measure training-position ranking sensitivity, explicitly labeled as training diagnostics. Validation perturbations require a separate optional audit hook supplied with permitted validation histories and the identical pinned candidate arrays; never infer validation HR from the training loader. Use local seeded generators, compact retained histories with unchanged padding conventions, and preserve original seen-item masks during catalog audits. Compare deletions with equal-count random controls and report residual positional and popularity confounding. Run order perturbations separately with the latest item fixed. Bootstrap paired user effects within each category before macro-averaging. Audit full-catalog recommendations only for the designated twenty training users, masking original histories and scoring in chunks. Keep all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and artifacts beneath the trial directory. No architecture or predictor changes are needed for this diagnostic-only idea. Diagnostics consume the shared search budget and should run at selected checkpoints.

originality.positive: Combines controlled history perturbations, explicit evidence boundaries, and architecture-compatible probes within the required adapter.
originality.negative: History ablation and sequence shuffling are established techniques; the contribution is primarily careful integration and interpretation.

future_potential.positive: Can guide subsequent recency scoring and sequence-model changes while separating training geometry from measured validation behavior.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity alone neither establishes user intent nor guarantees that an intervention will improve HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing scoring hooks and frozen checkpoints, requiring no additional model training or pretrained assets.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct candidate reuse, padding, seen-item masks, mode restoration, and paired statistical aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes original-versus-shuffled history comparisons across fifteen datasets.
Motivates measuring sequence-order dependence instead of assuming sequential structure.
limitations: Ranking sensitivity to shuffling does not establish current user intent.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary identifies item availability as a confound in ordinary sequence shuffling.
Motivates constrained perturbations that respect item first appearance.
limitations: Constrained controls require reliable temporal information.
Controlled order sensitivity still does not establish practical relevance or compatibility.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: sampled recommendation evaluation
contributions: Explains discrepancies between sampled ranking metrics and full-catalog evaluation.
Supports keeping catalog behavior audits separate from the pinned sampled-candidate selection metric.
limitations: Does not justify modifying this task's fixed evaluator.
Does not provide evidence that a particular diagnostic improves recommendation quality.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Product Recommendation Task Definitions
contributions: Separates substitutes, complements, related products, and compatibility judgments.
Supports distinguishing unknown compatibility from explicit conflict.
limitations: A task taxonomy does not supply missing item specifications or user ownership information.
Applying compatibility flags requires independently validated extraction rules.
